Mesoscale Discussion 1868
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0454 PM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

   Areas affected...Ohio into western Pennsylvania

   Concerning...Severe potential...Watch unlikely 

   Valid 082154Z - 090000Z

   Probability of Watch Issuance...5 percent

   SUMMARY...Thunderstorms may increase in coverage over the next
   couple of hours, and could pose a risk for damaging winds, and
   perhaps large hail, over parts of Ohio and western Pennsylvania.
   However, the coverage of intense/severe thunderstorms should be
   sufficiently limited to preclude watch issuance.

   DISCUSSION...Convection has been slowly intensifying along a diffuse
   cold front from the northern shores of Lake Erie southwestward into
   western OH. So far most of this convection has largely been shallow
   with only occasional updraft pulses strong enough to produce
   lightning. However, with time the expectation is that continued
   forcing along the approaching front, combined with gradually
   deepening cold pools (especially where storm clustering can occur),
   should support adequate lift for intensification of a few
   cells/clusters within an otherwise buoyant and weakly capped
   environment. Regional VWPs are sampling mid-level winds between
   30-35 knots, which should yield effective bulk shear values of
   around 25 knots - sufficient for some degree of storm organization.
   Consequently, a severe storm or two capable of producing damaging
   gusts and perhaps small to marginally severe hail may emerge from
   this regime over the next couple of hours. In general, the weak
   forcing for ascent should limit the coverage of strong/severe
   storms, and the onset of nocturnal cooling after 00 UTC should
   temporally constrain the severe threat to the next few hours. Given
   these limitations, watch issuance appears unlikely.

   ..Moore/Mosier.. 08/08/2026

Mesoscale Discussion 1867
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0453 PM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

   Areas affected...portions of northern Kansas

   Concerning...Severe potential...Watch unlikely 

   Valid 082153Z - 082330Z

   Probability of Watch Issuance...20 percent

   SUMMARY...A couple instances of severe gusts or perhaps some hail
   may accompany any of the stronger storms that manage to sustain
   themselves through the remainder of the afternoon.

   DISCUSSION...A lone multicellular cluster has matured over northern
   KS in the past hour, likely driven by the intersection of a strongly
   heated/mixed boundary layer and weak surface convergence along a
   baroclinic boundary. A belt of 15-20 kt southerly low-level flow is
   in place across the Plains, overspread by 30+ kt 500 mb
   northwesterlies, resulting in 40+ kts of effective bulk shear over
   northern KS. The baroclinic boundary precedes the ongoing
   multicellular cluster, where surface dewpoints exceed 70 F, yielding
   over 3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Nonetheless, forcing for ascent is weak in
   this region, casting great uncertainty on the coverage and overall
   longevity of any severe threat. Current visible satellite does not
   suggest any imminent threat for additional convective development in
   the near term. Still, given adequate vertical wind shear and
   instability, a conditional threat for a few severe gusts and perhaps
   an instance of severe hail may accompany this multicellular cluster,
   assuming it persists along the baroclinic boundary.

   ..Squitieri/Mosier.. 08/08/2026
